pass_1: golden_v1.jsonl (manually adjudicated by the project author)
caveat: Pass 1 was manually adjudicated by the project author. Pass 2 was produced by a model, so this is a human-versus-model sensitivity check, not inter-annotator agreement between two people.

disagreements.customer_msg: So has been sending me random other people's packages and their support has been worse than useless.
disagreements.pass_1_note: Two distinct problems, other people's packages arriving and support failing, with no specific ask, which the boundary rule sends here.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is reporting receiving packages belonging to others and expresses dissatisfaction with support, indicating a significant issue requiring human intervention.

disagreements.customer_msg: Help So #disappointed Ordered a prime phone, should have been here yesterday but tracking just says delayed until Friday.
disagreements.pass_1_note: Delayed but still expected, and tracking already carries the new date. A grounded delay reply is safe.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is expressing disappointment about a late delivery and requesting information on its status.

disagreements.customer_msg: You know me waiting on this delivery is preventing me from doing uni work. If I fail, Amazon is to blame🙄🙄🙄
disagreements.pass_1_note: Still waiting, still expected. Standard delivery-window answer is safe.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer expresses frustration and blames Amazon for academic consequences, indicating a negative support experience.

disagreements.customer_msg: I'm a Prime Business customer, and facing problem placing orders. It's really a pity that your system still doesn't support different shipping+billing address (
disagreements.pass_1_note: A Prime Business system limitation, separate shipping and billing addresses. Product feedback that no class covers.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is expressing frustration with a system limitation and not directly contesting a charge.

disagreements.customer_msg: 'gift wrapping'. It doesn't quite say gift - or wrapped. Box was cracked and the tape is so sticky it's ripped the presentation packaging. <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: Gift wrapping that arrived cracked and torn. The packaging-feedback reply is safe in public.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The message describes damage to packaging and includes a URL, requiring human review for potential security or further details.

disagreements.customer_msg: just had to make a complaint regarding wrong item sent to me. Have to say your customer service is fantastic!!
disagreements.pass_1_note: Reads as sarcasm about the support experience; the brand took it literally. Ambiguous either way, so a human should read it.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The message is praise for the brand and does not constitute a support request.

disagreements.customer_msg: seriously?! A massive box just for an item 2mm thick?! Stop killing the rainforests!! <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: Over-packaging complaint, which this class covers.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The message expresses frustration and criticism of packaging practices but does not constitute a support request or fall into any defined category.

disagreements.customer_msg: How do I buy prime membership as a gift? I want to buy Prime + a Echo as a Christmas gift?
disagreements.pass_1_note: Pre-sales question about gifting a Prime membership. No account-access issue at all, and the taxonomy has no pre-sales class.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is asking about purchasing a digital service (Prime) and device (Echo) as a gift, which falls outside the defined categories.

disagreements.customer_msg: I received my order today and one of the books is damaged. <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: One damaged book in an otherwise fine order, reported calmly. The return and replacement options reply is safe.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer explicitly states the item is damaged and provides a URL for evidence.

disagreements.customer_msg: this is ridiculous! My drum head came in a broken box and is warped and ripped <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: Item arrived warped in a broken box. The available-options reply is the brand's own standard answer.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer explicitly describes damage to the item and packaging.

disagreements.customer_msg: When are we going to get suits 7 on ???
disagreements.pass_1_note: Prime Video content availability, which this class covers explicitly. Not off-topic chatter.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is asking about the delivery status of 'suits 7', but provides no context regarding order number or other identifying information. This requires human investigation.

disagreements.customer_msg: when do you guys charge for the Xbox one X I preordered? It ships the 6th.
disagreements.pass_1_note: A question about when a pre-order is charged. There is no dispute, so billing_charge_dispute does not apply, and no class covers charge timing.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is asking about a charge related to a pre-order, but the nature of the charge isn't specified. This requires investigation.

disagreements.customer_msg: ALL of the video streaming apps look like garbage on the new 2017 Fire TV.. I even restored to factory, and no difference.
disagreements.pass_1_note: Streaming apps rendering badly on a Fire TV after a factory reset. Asking for more detail is safe in public.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is reporting a specific issue with a device (Fire TV) and its functionality, falling under the scope of digital service support.

disagreements.customer_msg: When Amazon tells you your package is arriving today before 8 pm but it hasn't even arrived at/left the carrier facility. Ugh 😑 <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: The package has not left the carrier facility, so it is in transit and merely going to be late.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer expresses frustration and disbelief regarding a missed delivery window, indicating potential anger or distress.

disagreements.customer_msg: is it standard protocol for your delivery drivers to knock on the door or ring the bell when delivering? He didn’t 🤔
disagreements.pass_1_note: A policy question about driver conduct. No wrong-location claim is made, which delivery_wrong_location requires.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is asking about delivery protocol, not a problem with a delivery.

disagreements.customer_msg: my partner has had bad service at the moment. Parcel was suppose to arrive saturday had a delay notice, then would be here today. Still no parcel! This was supp
disagreements.pass_1_note: The grievance is explicitly framed as paying extra for Prime and still waiting, which is the boundary this class turns on rather than simple lateness.
disagreements.pass_2_note: Customer expresses frustration and anger regarding a late delivery despite paying for Prime.

disagreements.customer_msg: , Alexa couldn't find any songs when asked to "Play Hindi Party Songs" on Echo2 😑
disagreements.pass_1_note: Alexa cannot find a requested music category on an Echo. Routine device troubleshooting.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is reporting a specific issue with a digital service (Alexa) and its functionality, requiring investigation.

disagreements.customer_msg: Preordered Sonic Forces so we can get it today - Amazon said it's not even dispatched?! Wtf why do this to me >:(
disagreements.pass_1_note: Pre-order not yet dispatched but still expected. Frustrated wording, no abuse, and the delivery-estimate answer is safe in public.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer expresses frustration and disbelief regarding a non-dispatched pre-order.

disagreements.customer_msg: Vai ter promoção do Kindle ???
disagreements.pass_1_note: Genuine pre-sales question about Kindle discounts, not promotional chatter. No class covers pricing or promotions. Also Portuguese.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The message is asking about a promotion and does not express a support need or complaint.

disagreements.customer_msg: What I ordered vs what it came in. Literally a tiny fob watch. Slow clap You're wrong for the #environment. Do better! But thanks for making it recyclable at le
disagreements.pass_1_note: Over-packaging complaint with a photo, which this class covers.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer received a significantly different item than ordered and expressed dissatisfaction with the packaging, indicating a problem beyond a simple mis-shipment.

disagreements.customer_msg: so it's acceptable to send parcels with NO packaging now is it?! Well done for ruining Christmas presents! I'm so angry.
disagreements.pass_1_note: Packaging failure that ruined Christmas presents. The customer says outright they are angry.
disagreements.pass_2_note: Customer expresses extreme anger and dissatisfaction with the service, indicating a significant negative experience.

disagreements.customer_msg: Hey, ! Lester’s not called me back! Is he still waiting for to reply? <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: A promised callback from a named agent never came, so the customer has already been failed once.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is reporting a missing delivery and requesting information about its status.

disagreements.customer_msg: Why did I pay for one day shipping from and it takes 2 days?
disagreements.pass_1_note: Disputes a paid one-day shipping promise rather than asking where a parcel is, which is the boundary this class turns on.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer expresses frustration with the delivery time exceeding expectations.

disagreements.customer_msg: Hey amazon. You decided to refund an order instead of replacing it but didn't bother to refund the full amount (import fees) of an item I didn't even get!?!? Th
disagreements.pass_1_note: Chasing the unpaid portion of an agreed refund, and angry about it.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer disputes an incorrect refund and the item remains listed, indicating a complex billing issue requiring investigation.

disagreements.customer_msg: Thanks I recycled your box into a Halloween costume. #halloween <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: Friendly chatter about reusing a box, no support request.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The message is purely promotional and does not represent a support request or complaint.

disagreements.customer_msg: Phone number provided to website isn't working right now, so I cannot connect to the courier facility. Any help?
disagreements.pass_1_note: A broken courier contact number. Nothing to do with account access, and no class covers contact-channel failures.
disagreements.pass_2_note: Customer is unable to access a website feature (courier facility) and requires assistance.

disagreements.customer_msg: Shocking packaging, is this how you package all your hard drives ? <URL>
disagreements.pass_1_note: Packaging-quality complaint with no explicit ask, which this class covers.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer explicitly describes damaged packaging and provides a URL for visual evidence; this is not a standard complaint category.

disagreements.customer_msg: . I guess it was some new definition of "delivering today" that I wasn't previously aware of.
disagreements.pass_1_note: Sarcastic but routine: the parcel missed its promised day and is still expected.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer expresses disbelief about the delivery status without providing specific details or location information.

disagreements.customer_msg: is it usual practice to cut off calls to customers as u av failed twice in a week to deliver prime? Very rude!!!!!
disagreements.pass_1_note: Subject is the support experience itself (calls cut off), not the delivery.
disagreements.pass_2_note: The customer is explicitly stating rudeness and disputing a paid Prime guarantee due to repeated failures.

action_kappa_warning: The two passes escalate at very different rates (66% vs 94%). Cohen's kappa on the action is therefore driven mostly by that prior and not by label ambiguity; read raw_agreement and action_confusion instead, and treat the intent kappa as the usable label-quality figure.
